subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of the following is a fossil fuel?
questions.explain: Coal, along with crude oil and natural gas, is a fossil fuel formed from the remains of ancient organisms.

questions.q: The three main fossil fuels are coal, crude oil and which other?
questions.explain: Coal, crude oil and natural gas are the three principal fossil fuels burnt to generate energy.

questions.q: Why are fossil fuels classed as non-renewable?
options: They take millions of years to form and are used faster than they can be replaced
They can be re-grown within a single year
They are made continuously in power stations
They never run out because they are recycled
questions.explain: Fossil fuels form over millions of years, so once used they cannot be practically replenished, making them finite.

questions.q: What is the main environmental problem caused by burning fossil fuels?
options: Release of carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas that contributes to climate change
Reduction of oxygen in the sea
Creation of ozone in the upper atmosphere
questions.explain: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas linked to global warming and climate change.

questions.q: Which fuel is used in a nuclear power station?
questions.explain: Nuclear power stations use uranium, which undergoes nuclear fission to release heat energy.

questions.q: What is one advantage of nuclear power compared with fossil-fuel power stations?
options: It does not release carbon dioxide while generating electricity
It produces no waste at all
It costs almost nothing to build
questions.explain: Nuclear fission generates electricity without burning fuel, so no carbon dioxide is produced during generation.

questions.q: What is a major disadvantage of nuclear power?
options: It produces radioactive waste that stays dangerous for a very long time
It releases large amounts of carbon dioxide
It relies on the weather to work
It cannot generate large amounts of electricity
questions.explain: Nuclear power creates radioactive waste that remains hazardous for many years and is difficult to store safely.

questions.q: Which of these is a renewable energy source?
questions.explain: Wind is a renewable source because it is naturally replenished and will not run out.

questions.q: Which device converts light energy directly into electrical energy?
questions.explain: Photovoltaic cells convert light energy from the Sun directly into electrical energy.

questions.q: How does a wind turbine generate electricity?
options: It converts the kinetic energy of moving air into electrical energy
It burns wind to release heat
It converts light energy into electricity
It stores chemical energy in cells
questions.explain: Moving air (kinetic energy) turns the turbine blades, which drive a generator to produce electricity.

questions.q: A design team wants to generate electricity for a site next to a fast-flowing mountain river. Which renewable source is most suitable?
questions.explain: Hydroelectric power uses fast-moving or falling water to turn turbines, ideal for a fast-flowing river.

questions.q: Which renewable source relies on the gravitational pull of the Moon and is therefore highly predictable?
questions.explain: Tides are caused by the Moon's gravitational pull, so tidal power output can be predicted accurately.

questions.q: Why is biomass considered a renewable energy source?
options: New plants and organic material can be grown to replace what is used
It is dug up from underground over millions of years
It never releases any carbon dioxide
questions.explain: Biomass comes from organic matter such as plants that can be re-grown, so it is replenishable.

questions.q: A remote off-grid cabin in a sunny location needs electricity without any fuel being delivered. Which renewable option is most appropriate?
questions.explain: Solar photovoltaic panels generate electricity from sunlight on site, needing no fuel deliveries or grid connection.

questions.q: In what form does a battery store energy?
questions.explain: A battery stores energy chemically and converts it into electrical energy when connected to a circuit.

questions.q: What is the difference between a primary cell and a secondary cell?
options: A primary cell is non-rechargeable while a secondary cell can be recharged
A primary cell is always larger than a secondary cell
A primary cell stores kinetic energy while a secondary cell stores light
A primary cell can be recharged while a secondary cell cannot
questions.explain: Primary cells (e.g. alkaline) are used once, whereas secondary cells (e.g. lithium-ion) can be recharged and reused.

questions.q: Which battery type is rechargeable and commonly used in mobile phones and laptops?
questions.explain: Lithium-ion cells are rechargeable secondary cells with a high energy density, used in phones and laptops.

questions.q: What happens to the total voltage when cells are connected in series?
options: The voltage stays the same but current halves
questions.explain: Connecting cells in series adds their voltages together, increasing the total supply voltage.

questions.q: A product needs a 6 V supply and uses 1.5 V AA cells. How should the cells be arranged?
questions.explain: Cells in series add their voltages, so 4 x 1.5 V = 6 V provides the required supply.

questions.q: A grid operator has surplus electricity at night and needs to store large amounts for peak daytime demand. Which storage method is designed for this?
questions.explain: Kinetic pumped storage pumps water uphill using surplus energy, then releases it to generate electricity at peak demand.
